_about: What Obelisk knows about Minecraft crashes and logs, written from community troubleshooting guides, mod issue trackers and loader docs. 'all'/'any' are lowercase substrings of the file; 'mods' must all be installed (mod ids); 'blame' names the mod to point at ($1 = the namespace found by 'blameFrom'). 'noise' entries mark log lines that look scary but are harmless.

problems.title: Sodium and Embeddium are both installed
problems.detail: Embeddium is a NeoForge copy of Sodium. Two renderers replacing the same game code will crash or render garbage.
problems.fix: Keep one. On 1.21+ NeoForge, Sodium itself works; remove Embeddium (and its add-ons like Embeddium++ or Rubidium Extra).

problems.title: OptiFine clashes with Sodium/Iris
problems.detail: OptiFine rewrites the same rendering code as Sodium, Embeddium and Iris. They can't run together.
problems.fix: Remove OptiFine. Sodium (speed) plus Iris (shaders) covers what OptiFine did.

problems.title: Connector is installed without Forgified Fabric API
problems.detail: Sinytra Connector runs Fabric mods on NeoForge, but almost every Fabric mod also needs Fabric API, which on NeoForge comes as Forgified Fabric API.
problems.fix: Install Forgified Fabric API from Browse.

any: could not reserve enough space for object heap
could not create the java virtual machine
problems.title: Java couldn't start with this much memory
problems.detail: The memory setting is more than Java can reserve. Usually the profile asks for more RAM than the PC has free, or a 32-bit Java is in use.
problems.fix: Lower Custom memory in Profile options (6–8 GB is plenty for most packs) and make sure the profile uses a 64-bit Java.

problems.title: The sound system crashed
problems.detail: The crash is in OpenAL, the library Minecraft plays sound through. It's usually a sound driver, a virtual audio device or Windows Spatial Sound.
problems.fix: Turn off Spatial Sound (Windows sound settings), unplug or switch away from virtual audio devices, and update the sound driver.

problems.title: The game's window library crashed
problems.detail: LWJGL/GLFW (the code that talks to your screen and graphics card) crashed. Overlays like RivaTuner, MSI Afterburner, Discord or OBS game capture are common triggers.
problems.fix: Close or turn off overlays, update the graphics driver, and try again.

problems.title: The graphics card ran out of memory
problems.detail: Video memory (VRAM) filled up. High-resolution resource packs, heavy shaders and long LOD/render distances all eat VRAM.
problems.fix: Lower render distance, LOD distance or shader quality, or use lower-resolution resource packs.

problems.title: Too many or too big textures for your graphics card
problems.detail: All block and item textures are stitched into one image, and it grew bigger than your graphics card allows.
problems.fix: Remove high-resolution (128x+) resource packs, or turn mipmaps down in Video Settings.

any: payload may not be larger than
problems.title: The game sent more data in one go than Minecraft allows
problems.detail: Big modpacks (many recipes, tags or items with lots of data) can go over Minecraft's packet size limits, which kicks you from the world or server.
problems.fix: Install Packet Fixer (or XL Packets) on both client and server.

problems.title: The connection to the world timed out
problems.detail: The (built-in) server took too long to answer. Usually a very slow world load or a frozen server tick.
problems.fix: Install Packet Fixer to raise the timeout, and see 'Where the time went' below for what was slow.

any: this server has mods that require
problems.title: Your mods don't match the server's
problems.detail: The server and this profile have different mods or versions, so they can't agree on blocks, items and network channels.
problems.fix: Use exactly the same mod list as the server (a server pack from Obelisk's right-click menu does this for your own packs).

problems.title: Your Minecraft sign-in expired
problems.detail: The account's session wasn't accepted.
problems.fix: Open Prism's accounts and refresh or re-add the account.

all: ksyxis: speeding up the world loading
problems.title: The world stopped loading after Ksyxis
problems.detail: Ksyxis skips spawn-chunk loading to make worlds open faster. Its own message says to remove it if loading gets stuck right after it.
problems.fix: If the world never opened, disable Ksyxis and try again.

problems.title: A world generation mod isn't thread-safe with C2ME
problems.detail: C2ME generates chunks on many threads at once. Some worldgen mods assume one thread and break when two chunks touch the same list.
problems.fix: Disable C2ME to confirm. If that fixes it, keep C2ME off or check C2ME's issue tracker for that mod.

problems.title: A world generation mod crashed while building terrain
problems.detail: The crash happened while generating new chunks (terrain, a structure or a feature).
problems.fix: Update the mod named below. Moving away from that spot or using a new world can avoid it until it's fixed.

problems.title: A creature or object crashed while being updated
problems.detail: Minecraft crashed while updating one entity (a mob, item frame, vehicle and so on). The crash report says which one.
problems.fix: Update the mod that adds it. If the world won't load, a mod like Neruina (or an entity-removal tool) can remove the broken entity.

problems.title: A block (machine, chest, spawner…) crashed while being updated
problems.detail: Minecraft crashed while updating one block entity. The crash report says which one and where.
problems.fix: Update the mod that adds it. If the world won't load, break that block with a tool like Neruina or an NBT editor.

problems.title: The game crashed while loading resources
problems.detail: The crash happened on the loading screen, while textures, models and sounds were loading. Usually one mod's resources are broken or two mods clash over the same models.
problems.fix: Check the mods named below; also try without resource packs.

problems.title: The game window couldn't open
problems.detail: The graphics driver couldn't give the game the OpenGL version it needs.
problems.fix: Update the graphics driver. On laptops, set javaw.exe to the high-performance GPU in Windows Graphics settings.

problems.title: A mod failed while starting up
problems.detail: A mod's setup code threw an error the first time it ran, so everything that depends on it fails too.
problems.fix: Update the mod named below, or check it's the build for your Minecraft and loader version.

problems.title: A mod uses code it isn't allowed to reach
problems.detail: Usually a mod built for a different Minecraft, loader or Java version.
problems.fix: Use the mod build made for your exact Minecraft and loader version.

problems.title: A mod points at a file it doesn't ship
problems.detail: A mod lists an access-transformer file it doesn't include. NeoForge skips it; it only matters if that mod misbehaves.

slow.note: RoadWeaver's GPU (OpenCL) path doesn't support this world's generation settings, so it plans roads on the CPU, which is much slower at world load.
Villager API re-validates every villager type and profession at startup and again at world load, even when no villager packs are installed.
Ksyxis prints this right before the world's spawn area is prepared; the wait after it is usually other mods' world setup (shown on the next line).
JEI indexes every item and recipe when you join. Huge packs take a few seconds; EMI or turning off JEI's ingredient list cache rebuild helps.
C2ME compiles world generation code the first time a world loads.
Minecraft saving the world. Big worlds or many loaded chunks make this longer.
Minecraft generating the spawn area. Fresh worlds with heavy worldgen mods take longest.
Loading textures, models and sounds. More mods and resource packs make this longer.
